summary: Tokyo is one of the easiest big-city trips with children — spotless public restrooms, baby-change rooms in every station and department store, affordable kid-friendly food everywhere. These are the picks that go beyond the usual.
tips: Strollers are manageable but crowded trains + long station staircases are hard — baby carriers win the commute.
Konbini (7-Eleven, Family Mart, Lawson) stock formula, diapers, baby food, toys.
Priority-seat cars on trains are for elderly, pregnant, and disabled passengers first — leave those empty at rush hour.
Most museums and attractions give under-6 free entry and half-price for ages 6-12.
Stations now sell 'babyroom' maps — clean breastfeeding and change rooms inside major stations and department stores.

picks.name: Tokyo Disneyland
picks.body: The most visited Disney park in Asia; more classic Americana than Shanghai or Hong Kong. Fantasyland and Toontown are built for young kids.
picks.tip: Book date-specific tickets online 60 days ahead; Disney Premier Access for the hottest rides. Weekday beats weekend 10x.

picks.name: Tokyo DisneySea
picks.body: Unique to Tokyo and arguably the best Disney park in the world — nautical-themed lands, higher-thrill rides, excellent food. Fantasy Springs opened 2024.
picks.tip: Better for older kids and adults. Mountain Beverage at Mount Prometheus tops every 'best Disney drink' list.

picks.name: KidZania Tokyo
picks.body: Kids-sized city where children 'work' real jobs (firefighter, pilot, sushi chef, radio DJ) and earn in-park currency. Completely in Japanese but most activities are visual and kids figure it out fast.
picks.tip: Book the earliest morning session. Sessions are 5-hour blocks; pack water and snacks for parents (food inside is limited).

picks.name: Ghibli Museum
picks.body: Half-day with under-10s. Climb-in Catbus, rotating short film in the basement theatre (you get a unique film strip ticket), rooftop Laputa robot.
picks.tip: Tickets open the 10th of the previous month at 10:00 JST on Lawson Loppi or JTB abroad. They sell in hours.

picks.name: Ueno Zoo
picks.body: Japan's oldest zoo, home to giant pandas (reliably the queue magnet). Well-sized for a half-day visit.
picks.tip: ¥600 adult, free under 12. Monorail between east and west zones. Pair with Ueno Park for a picnic afterwards.

picks.name: Shin-Yokohama Ramen Museum
picks.body: Replica 1958 Tokyo street with 9 famous regional ramen shops, a photo-op hit and a surprisingly good food hall. Kids' mini-ramen bowls let them try 3-4 styles without giving up.
picks.tip: ¥450 entry; each bowl ordered separately. Go before 11:00 to avoid the lunch queue.

picks.name: Odaiba waterfront
picks.body: Life-sized Unicorn Gundam statue (free, moves on the hour), small beach and Rainbow Bridge view, the Yurikamome train is driverless (sit in the front for kid-bliss). TeamLab Planets nearby.
picks.tip: Walk the Odaiba-to-Toyosu waterfront for easy stroller access. Sunset is the win.

picks.name: Shōwa Kinen Park
picks.body: 165-hectare park with a rainbow-coloured dragon jungle gym, trampoline meadows, cherry blossom avenues, a lake with pedal boats, kids' cycling courses.
picks.tip: Bike rental at the gate lets you cover more ground. Weekend afternoons only fill at peak sakura or autumn foliage.

picks.name: teamLab Planets
picks.body: Barefoot digital-art walk — koi projections swim around your legs, mirrored orchid room, ankle-deep water. Kids love it; strollers are not accommodated.
picks.tip: Wear clothes you can roll up to the knee. 75 minutes is enough.

picks.name: Tokyo Joypolis
picks.body: Sega-run indoor amusement park — VR coasters, Sonic attractions, rhythm games. Rainy-day saviour.
picks.tip: Day passports (~¥5,100 adult / ¥4,300 child) beat per-ride pricing if you're staying >2 hours.

picks.name: Origami Kaikan
picks.body: Free museum of origami and paper-making; drop-in folding sessions several times a week; gift shop is a paper lover's heaven.
picks.tip: Check the weekly workshop schedule online — English-friendly sessions run most weekends.

picks.name: The Railway Museum (Tetsudo Hakubutsukan)
picks.body: Full-size Shinkansen bullet trains you can climb into, driving simulators, diorama with 1,200 model trains. Train-loving kids will not leave quietly.
picks.tip: Buy tickets at konbini Loppi machines in advance; walk-ups can sell out on weekends.
